gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Expressive and a bit quirky, Tektur draws pipe-cleaner strokes with no pressure change. Noto Sans Kayah Li does the opposite job, lifting its brush-like ends away from each curve so running text feels softly handwritten rather than engineered.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Wire-bent and slightly futuristic, Tektur runs its monoline strokes from stem to finish. Noto Sans Kharoshthi takes over where text needs weight, laying a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through each line, with curves that never quite close.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Tektur has outsized lowercase and not a single hairline anywhere in its alphabet. Noto Sans Khmer, a sans-serif, keeps its small letters standing proud and notched open, so a long stretch of text stays easy on the eye.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Pipe-cleaner strokes with no thick-thin shifts make Tektur instantly recognizable. Noto Sans Khojki settles into a plain sans manner, its wide exits letting light through, so a long passage reads with a clear, open eye on every e.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Approachable is the last thing you'd expect from a heading this flat and unmodulated, yet Tektur manages it. Noto Sans Khudawadi follows with unsealed rounds and capitals barely taller than its lowercase, so both lines sit comfortably together.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-kr: Tektur's drafting-pen outlines, drawn with one constant nib width, give it a look unlike most display faces. Noto Sans KR is the sturdy partner.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-lao: Contemporary and a little mechanical, Tektur keeps its stems and arcs in lockstep for striking headings. Noto Sans Lao instead stretches its x-height tall.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Professional in manner yet oddly playful in outline, Tektur is flat and free of contrast, which suits big, short headings. And Noto Sans Lao Looped makes words read as solid blocks, with bowls left open on one side.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Approachable despite its engineered look, Tektur bends rounded-wire strokes into curves with generous terminal openings and oversized lowercase. Noto Sans Lepcha reads sturdily, its lowercase standing like cast iron capitals.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Contemporary and unfussy, Tektur has no thick-thin swing at all, just bent wire with outsized lowercase. Noto Sans Limbu follows with tall-bodied small letters and gaping curves, giving the heading a roomier, more open companion beneath it.
